summary_rationale: Texas Instruments operates one of the highest-quality franchises in global semiconductors: an ~80,000-product Analog and Embedded Processing catalog serving 100,000+ customers across Industrial (33%), Automotive (33%), Personal Electronics (21%), and Data Center (9%), with >80% of revenue flowing through direct channels including TI.com. Its multi-year 300mm wafer fab buildout (RFAB1/RFAB2, LFAB1/LFAB2, SM1/SM2) creates a durable ~40% die-level cost advantage over 200mm peers and targets >95% internal wafer production by 2030. After enduring a two-year industrial/automotive destocking downturn (FY2023-FY2024) alongside peak fab capex ($5.07B in 2023, $4.82B in 2024, $4.55B in 2025), the business inflected sharply in 2026: Q3 2026 revenue jumped 28% YoY to $6.06B, gross margin rebounded from 57.0% in FY2025 to 64.2%, capex stepped down toward the $2B-$3B framework, and TTM free cash flow surged to $8.42B (aided by $1.6B in CHIPS Act incentives). Watch items remain: elevated inventory (194 days in Q3 2026, down from 241 days at end-2024), $13.65B gross debt ahead of the $7.5B all-cash Silicon Labs acquisition (expected H1 2027 close), and intensifying Chinese domestic substitution in general-purpose analog.
